<Rep. Nydia M. Velázquez>: The Small Business Administration (SBA) offers a variety of services to help educate and counsel small businesses, including Small Business Development Centers (SBDCs) and Women's Business Centers (WBCs).
• With over 900 locations nationwide, SBDCs
provide valuable resources to small businesses across
the country, including networking, counseling, and
training. Through a partnership with SBA, SBDCs are
hosted by universities, colleges, state economic
development agencies, or private entities, and their
goal is to help launch and grow small businesses. In
Fiscal Year 2023, SBDCs served nearly 326,000 unique
small business clients, contributing to nearly 21,000
new business starts and supporting over 1,303,000
jobs.\1\
\1\U.S. Small Bus. Admin., FY 2025 Congressional Budget Justification & FY 2023 Annual Performance Report, 95-96 (Mar. 11, 2024).
• WBCs have more than 140 centers across the
country that offer a wide variety of services to women
business owners, which include personalized counseling
and training, classes, and technical assistance. Many
WBCs offer flexible hours, including weekends and
evenings, to allow mothers to attend programs and
obtain services. In Fiscal Year 2023, WBCs served
87,900 unique small business clients, contributing to
over 3,400 new business starts.\2\
\2\Id at 96-97.
Small firms have faced issues related to attracting and retaining a skilled workforce. Career and technical education (CTE) opportunities provide a competitive and practical career path and can help address the current labor and skills shortage. At the Committee's February 5, 2025 hearing titled ``Hope on the Horizon: Prioritizing Small Business Growth in the 119th Congress,'' Karl Hutter, CEO of Nevada aerospace part manufacturer Click Bond, Inc., testified that CTE was ``essential'' to addressing the shortage in skilled labor for small businesses like his.\3\ Moreover, SBDCs and WBCs can be valuable resource partners in supporting small businesses in meeting their labor needs and finding skilled workers.
\3\Hope on the Horizon: Prioritizing Small Business Growth in the 119th Congress: Hearing Before the H. Comm. on Small Bus., 119th Cong. (Feb. 2, 2025).
Nydia M. Velazquez,
Ranking Member.
